"I don’t think it was an end; I think it was really the end of Heisenberg’s journey," he said in the clip. "But I don’t think that was the end of Skyler and Walt and Holly’s journey. You know I think there’s a lot of unanswered questions there, that for them will probably never be answered."

 "I think there’s still a big step for the White family," Mitte added. 

Mitte also admitted that "Breaking Bad," which is widely considered one of the greatest TV shows of all time, set an almost impossible standard for the rest of his career.

"I just want to top ‘Breaking Bad,’ that’s the hardest," he said. "That is literally said, a bar for myself as a young man that is kinda unattainable. I tell people, ‘Look, it’s a long way down from the top of the mountain."

item.title: Harry Styles addresses ICE shooting in New York with call for ‘dignity and justice’
item.description: Harry Styles urged Madison Square Garden fans to show compassion and justice for Oscar Belgal after the ICE shooting sparked protests in New York City.
item.content:encoded:
Harry Styles paused his concert at Madison Square Garden in New York City on Saturday to address the shooting of a Dominican immigrant by federal immigration agents, urging fans to show compassion toward people from different backgrounds and calling for "dignity" and "justice."

The British pop star addressed the crowd after referencing Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old man who was shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers Thursday while his 5-year-old son was sitting in the back seat of his car.

"I just want us to take a moment to think about Oscar Belgal tonight, and I want us to think and remember to just look after each other," Styles said.

"So, please, continue looking after each other," he continued. "And remember, your friends, the people you love, the people who don't look like you and aren't born where you're from, they deserve respect, and love, and dignity and justice."

PARAMORE'S HAYLEY WILLIAMS LAUNCHES VULGAR TIRADE AT DHS AFTER AGENCY DEFENDS ICE OFFICERS

The remarks prompted criticism from film critic and commentator Christian Toto, who told Fox News Digital that speaking out against ICE has become a way for celebrities to gain approval within the entertainment industry.

"This is the new black square on Instagram — speaking out on ICE gets you respect within your artistic community and endless positive press," Toto said. "I think the mainstream media has far more impact on public opinion. Social media does, too. Celebrities weighing in on matters like this? I suspect it doesn't move the needle at all. We view the stars as detached from our day-to-day lives, so we may agree with them on hot-button issues but they're not winning any converts."

He suggested that entertainers face pressure within Hollywood to embrace political causes, while those who remain silent may be better positioned to avoid alienating fans.

"There's an expectation within celebrity circles to embrace the cause du jour. The benefits are clear, and they're never held responsible when history doesn't align with their views. I suspect the stars who don't speak out at all fare best with their fans," Toto said.

OLIVIA WILDE BREAKS SILENCE ON HARRY STYLES FANS AND THEIR BRUTAL REACTION TO THEIR 10-YEAR AGE GAP ROMANCE

Styles' comments came as the shooting of Belgal sparked protests and criticism from New York officials, including Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Belgal was shot after allegedly refusing to comply with officers conducting a targeted arrest operation, Fox News Digital reported. Federal officials said he accelerated his vehicle toward agents, prompting them to open fire. During a Thursday night news conference, Mamdani said he personally urged Trump to release Belgal and condemned the federal immigration agency.

"We know that ICE is rotten to its core. Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known..." Mamdani said.

MAMDANI SAYS EVEN IF HE CAN GET ALONG WITH TRUMP, HE STILL DEMANDS THAT 'ICE SHOULD BE ABOLISHED'

Marcos Charles, a senior ICE official, defended the shooting during a Friday news conference alongside Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, saying officers believed their lives were in danger.

"Our officers, using their training and believing that their life and the life of the partners and the general public were in danger, used their training and fired weapons," Charles said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Officials said agents were unaware that Belgal's son was inside the vehicle. The child was unharmed.

The Department of Homeland Security said Belgal had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests for assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. Federal officials also alleged ties to the Trinitarios street gang.

A federal judge temporarily blocked Belgal's deportation Friday while his legal challenge to detention proceeds, and the New York Police Department released body camera footage showing the aftermath of the shooting.

item.title: Yes, the SEC is still getting ridiculous preferential treatment in the AP Top 25 Poll
item.description: Texas dropped five spots after losing to unranked Oklahoma, while Alabama didn't budge after a home loss to Georgia in the latest AP Top 25 Poll.
item.content:encoded:
It's getting ridiculous. Well, it's past ridiculous.

The SEC, somehow, keeps getting preferential treatment in the AP Top 25 Poll in a way no other conference does. For some reason. And this week's poll might be the best example yet of how the bias among poll voters continues to impact the college football season.

Let's look at how the voters handled some of the biggest results of the weekend, compared to how they handled previous results from teams with the wrong patch on the front of their jersey.

WEEK 6 AP TOP 25 POLL SEES A MAJOR MIXUP AND A NEW TOP TEAM IN THE COUNTRY AFTER AN UPSET-FILLED SATURDAY

To start, we can look at the Texas-Oklahoma game. While the Longhorns outgained the Sooners both in total yardage and yards per play, they were set back by two terrible fourth quarter interceptions from quarterback Arch Manning. Both at the worst possible time. One was returned for a touchdown, and the other effectively allowed Oklahoma to win the game in regulation.

The Sooners were not ranked entering the week, and for good reason. They lost on the road to Michigan, scored just 14 points against New Mexico, and were blown out by Georgia 41-13. They're not a very good team. Texas may have outplayed them, but the very clear flaws in Manning's game cost them the result. A neutral site game against a middling unranked team that scored 14 points at home against New Mexico. The punishment for the Longhorns? Dropping from No. 1 to No. 7.

When Ohio State lost as the No. 1 team in the country, on the road to the then-No. 4 Longhorns by one point after a miraculous comeback, they dropped from No. 1 to No. 6. Similar punishments for wildly different "quality" losses.

Then there's Alabama.

The Crimson Tide lost, at home, to the Georgia Bulldogs in a close game, though the Bulldogs averaged a whopping 7.5 yards per play to just 5.8 for Alabama. Though the Tide were denied a clear and obvious pass interference penalty in the fourth quarter that may have changed the game.

Still, it's a home loss. Yes, Georgia is good, and yes, the score was close, but poll voters typically punish any team for losing a home game. And remember, Ohio State lost on the road to the presumptive No. 1 team in the country and dropped five spots.

Not Alabama! Remarkably, the Tide didn't budge, going from No. 6 to...No. 6. After losing. At home. Why even play the games when they don't matter?

Ole Miss has received some exceptional SEC treatment too. The Rebels resume now looks worse and worse, thanks largely to Florida and LSU's poor play. The Gators went from the darlings of college football to deservedly unranked in just a few weeks after an embarrassing blowout loss at home to South Carolina. The same Florida team that dominated Ole Miss 52-28, scoring 35 points in the second half. LSU, meanwhile, lost on the road to an unranked Kentucky team, their second of the season.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

So Ole Miss' big win now looks less impressive, and their loss went from "another quality blowout SEC road loss" to an indefensible blowout against a mediocre team. They entered the week at No. 9 in the AP Poll and after their resume took a huge hit, fell all the way to...No. 9.

What about LSU?

The Tigers spent a small fortune, at least $150 million, on hiring Lane Kiffin and revamping their roster. Thus far, they have an unimpressive 4-2 record to show for it, and with more tough games coming, an 8-4 finish might be the best case scenario. Two losses, no meaningful wins, and the Tigers somehow are still ranked No. 22.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Meanwhile, the Oregon Ducks have a win over a ranked team, No. 19 USC, and their two losses are to No. 18 Oklahoma State and No. 12 UCLA. Unranked. In fact, they're nearly 200 "points" behind the Tigers. Tennessee's big win this year is losing by three to Texas, yet they're ahead of other comparable one-loss teams.

Why does this matter? Well, there's a clear and obvious advantage this list gives the SEC: ranked wins and ranked losses. Tennessee plays Alabama this week, a ridiculous No. 6-No. 14 game. What should be two teams in the No. 10 and No. 20 range now looks much more important. LSU inexplicably staying in the polls at No. 22 allows this weekend's contest against Mississippi State to be another "ranked" game. Meanwhile, Nebraska, who's 5-1 with one close home loss to Indiana, is playing Oregon while both are unranked.

The polls determine strength of schedule, instead of more objective measurements, which is then used to inform arguments over the College Football Playoff field. The assumption, as always, is that the SEC has unmatched "depth" because of their brand names, marketing, and home stadiums.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

In reality, SP+, an analytics-based ranking system housed at ESPN that compares teams' success and efficiency on offense, defense, and special teams, then adjusts for opponent, has seven SEC teams in the top-25, and nine from the Big Ten. In fact, there are six Big 12 teams in the SP+ top-25, should we be talking about the gauntlet of playing in that conference?

Despite years of underperformance in the playoff, poll voters just can't stop thinking it's the mid-2010's and Nick Saban is somehow coaching all 16 SEC teams. It's time to move on from the marketing and start accepting reality.

item.title: A cross country runner switched to the girls team midseason, parents voice their disapproval at meet
item.description: A Camas High cross country runner switched from the boys team to the girls team midseason, sparking national debate over transgender athletes in sports.
item.content:encoded:
"Nobody wants to talk to you. I'm trying to be nice."

That was the not-so-nice greeting I got from a Camas High assistant cross country coach in Arlington, Washington on Saturday. It came as I stood near the start line for the Women's Elite 5k race at the Nike Hole in the Wall High School XC Invitational.

All I had done at that point was try to introduce myself, but it was clear that everybody involved with the school was on guard. The reason? One of the Camas runners entered in the Women's Elite 5K was a biological male.

AMERICANS CLASH OVER TRANSGENDER ATHLETES AS DEBATE HEATS UP: ‘JUST GETTING OUTRAGEOUS'

What's unique about this particular trans athlete is that he started the year on the boys team — with which he finished 76th in a JV race — then switched to the girls team last month. He has since taken first place in a varsity meet and finished second in a different invitational.

This, as you might imagine, has sparked national attention, putting everyone at Camas on the defensive. But that assistant was wrong about one thing: Lots of people — mainly parents from opposing schools — wanted to talk to me.

"We're about as liberal as it gets. I just don't agree with that [boys competing against girls]. I mean, if they find your body in 300 years, what are they going to say you were," said Kent Lake of Lake Stevens, WA. "Look, you can live any way you want. You got my blessing. But I mean come on, in competitions? It's like stock car racing. It's gotta be even, and it's gotta be fair."

What prompted the Camas runner to switch from the boys to the girls team remains unclear. No Camas coach would talk (although one, along with a school administrator, was gracious to me), and the boy's mother wouldn't acknowledge my presence Saturday.

WASHINGTON TRANS ATHLETE'S SCHOOL DISTRICT RESPONDS TO ALLEGED ASSAULT VICTIM'S SCOTUS INJUNCTION REQUEST

But such a switch is permitted under the rules of the Washington Interscholastic Activities Association (WIAA), which governs high school sports in the state. That doesn't mean most parents like it.

"When I first heard about this story, I was like, 'Is this real? That can't be real'," said a mother of a cross country runner, who requested anonymity. She argued that allowing transgender runners to compete against girls could deprive female athletes of victories they otherwise would have earned. "We have daughters, and it's robbing them of an opportunity to compete."

I LOST A STATE CHAMPIONSHIP TO A BOY. I REFUSE TO LOSE MY VOICE

It should be noted that the Camas runner isn't a star, even among girls. He finished 39th in a field of 135 in Saturday's race with a time of 18:36.8. But had he run in the Men's Elite 5K, he would have placed last out of 159 runners by a good 30 seconds.

Said one parent, also requesting anonymity. "Whether they finish first, 40th or 90th, they're still taking the spot of a girl."

The anonymous route is the one that most chose last Saturday. One man wouldn't even let me record his voice — I had to repeat his quote into my phone using my own voice. This, after all, may be the most sensitive, contentious issue there is in sports. And ... not all the parents at Saturday's meet were necessarily against the Camas runner.

One said, "People can identify however they want. High school sports isn't about winning, it's about student athletes building confidence."

Another said, "There are more important things in sports than that [issue]."

A third said, "I just wish people could have more empathy and compassion and understanding for people. I do think it's tricky if you start on one team and midseason change. I wish there was a space for everyone."

Most, however, were like Kevin Ess, an Arlington High parent who had a compassionate but firm take on the matter.

"I think men and women, young men and young women, have been competing for hundreds of years, thousands of years, separately," Ess said. "I think it's an interesting experiment. I think it's an interesting topic, but my personal opinion is that they should continue to compete separately."

ATTORNEY FOR ALLEGED VICTIM OF TRANS ATHLETE SEXUAL ASSAULT SAYS SCOTUS FIGHT CAN HELP SET TITLE IX PRECEDENT

One father said something similar after lifting his hoodie to reveal the XX-XY shirt he was sporting underneath.

Another said allowing boys to compete with girls was "stupid" and that "Title IX was designed to protect women."

A mother said, "I would be so embarrassed to put my son in a position like this." And though part of me agrees with that last part, part of me also wonders if it's a little harsh.

I was genuinely curious about what the past few weeks have been like for the Camas runner's parents, but the mother completely ignored me on two separate attempts to talk. This was the same woman who reportedly started recording an athlete who protested the Camas runner last month by walking off the start line when the gun went off.

That athlete was Skyview High junior Charlie Garrett, who staged the walk-off alongside teammate Sierra Retzlaff. Both wore body paint saying "Keep women in women's sports" that mid-September day — and both were on hand at Saturday's event as well.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Why is it so important for you to speak out on this topic?"

Retzlaff said: "Because if we don't, no one else will. If we start something, maybe others will have the courage to join."

Fortunately, there have been other girls and women who have spoken on this issue from Washington state and beyond. In fact, such courage helped get Initiative 638 — which would ban biological males from competing against girls in K-12 sports — on the Nov. 3 ballot in Washington state.

The situation in Camas could very well mobilize people to vote.

As one mother said Saturday: "There needs to be more work done to change the law, because schools are kind of tied to what the law is telling them to do. People need to get out and vote for what they want."

item.title: DNC Chair Ken Martin defends 'Big Tent' strategy when pressed on democratic socialists
item.description: Democratic Party Chairman Ken Martin says embracing a big-tent coalition, including DSA voices, is key to winning ahead of the midterm elections.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic National Committee Chairman Ken Martin defended his party's big-tent approach Monday, arguing Democrats must continue expanding their coalition even as Republicans target the party over its ties to democratic socialists.

Martin was pressed during an interview on MSNOW about whether the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is a liability for the party ahead of the midterm elections.

"So let me just say, I've always taken a big-tent approach to how you build a party," Martin said. "That's why I was successful for all these years in Minnesota. I believe you win through addition, not subtraction. You win by growing your coalition, not shrinking it."

NEWSOM TELLS DEMOCRATS TO BE IN THE 'ADDITION NOT SUBTRACTION' BUSINESS WITH SOCIALISTS

"And sometimes, is there a middle ground, though, when Americans see that…" interjected MSNOW anchor Peter Alexander.

"No, not at all, because that's where the vast majority of Americans are at," Martin replied. "Maybe right in the middle, or a little center-left, or a little center-right. But it doesn't mean we can't bring new voices into the party, right? Of course, we have to keep growing and we have to keep expanding this tent," Martin reiterated.

SEE IT: TOP DEM OPERATIVE DRAWS LINE AT ‘DEPLORABLE’ HASAN PIKER AFTER TOUTING PARTY’S ‘BIG TENT’

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Democratic National Committee for comment.

"Democratic Party Chair Ken Martin embraces far-Left radicals who want to abolish the police, prisons, and borders," the Republican National Committee wrote on X.

DSA CO-CHAIR MOCKED FOR PROUDLY CONFIRMING SOCIALISTS WANT TO ABOLISH THE SENATE, NATIONAL BORDERS, PRISONS
